question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}{{f}^{″}({x}_{n})},
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ and ${f}^{″}({x}_{n})$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n},$ respectively.

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =({x}^{4}-2{x}^{2}+x-5)^{′} \\  & =4{x}^{3}-4x+1, \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =(4{x}^{3}-4x+1)^{′} \\  & =12{x}^{2}-4 \\  & =4(3{x}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{4{x}_{n}^{3}-4{x}_{n}+1}{4(3{x}_{n}^{2}-1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1.8,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{4{x}_{0}^{3}-4{x}_{0}+1}{4(3{x}_{0}^{2}-1)} \\  & =1.8-\frac{4(1.8)^{3}-4(1.8)+1}{4(3(1.8)^{2}-1)} \\  & ≈1.309,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
